verdict.rationale: Vercel documents its own test environments that sit outside production. It creates automatic preview environments for testing changes before production. It manages environment variables separately for local, preview and production, so previews can point at non-production data sources. Vercel Sandbox runs agent-generated code in isolated microVMs. However, no documentation says preview or sandbox runs are guaranteed not to touch production data. That separation depends on the user configuring separate variables, and data branching comes only from a marketplace partner. missing for 10: first-party guarantee of production-data isolation for previews and sandboxes, built-in non-production data provisioning or branching, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: automatic preview environments for testing changes before production
Manage local, preview, production, and custom environments and the variables each one uses.
Run untrusted or agent-generated code in isolated Linux microVMs.
It can use secure sandboxes to reproduce issues, validate generated code, and run checks before suggested changes reach production.
